# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Terranova_2013_drugC1_gemcitabine_mouse"))$reference`
* Article: [Cancer Chemother Pharmacol. 2013;72(2):471-482](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-013-2208-8) (open access; PMC3718992)

Terranova et al. extended the single-agent Simeoni tumor-growth-inhibition
(TGI) model to two co-administered anticancer drugs. Each drug moves
proliferating tumor cells into its own chain of three damaged-cell states, a
cell can be hit by the second drug at any stage of the first drug's chain (a
four-by-four grid of states), and one extra parameter, gamma, moves
proliferating cells directly into the doubly damaged state at a rate
`gamma * Ca * Cb`. Positive gamma means synergy, negative gamma antagonism and
zero the purely additive ("zero-interaction") prediction.

The paper applied the model to six xenograft experiments, each analysed
separately with its own tumor and drug parameters, so each is its own model
file. The four investigational compounds are coded by the authors (Drug C1, an
Aurora kinase inhibitor; Drug C2, a polo-like kinase inhibitor; Drug C4 and
Drug C5, multikinase inhibitors) and have no disclosed INN.

| Model file | Experiment | Cell line | Drug a | Drug b |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Terranova_2013_drugC1_gemcitabine_mouse` | a | BxPC3 (pancreas) | Drug C1, IV | gemcitabine, IV |
| `Terranova_2013_drugC1_cisplatin_mouse` | b | A2780 (ovary) | Drug C1, IV | cisplatin, IV |
| `Terranova_2013_drugC2_irinotecan_mouse` | c | HT29 (colon) | Drug C2, oral | irinotecan, IV |
| `Terranova_2013_drugC2_fluorouracil_mouse` | d | HT29 (colon) | Drug C2, oral | 5-fluorouracil, IV |
| `Terranova_2013_drugC4_gemcitabine_mouse` | e | BxPC3 (pancreas) | Drug C4, oral | gemcitabine, IV |
| `Terranova_2013_drugC5_irinotecan_mouse` | f | HT29 (colon) | Drug C5, IV | irinotecan, IV |

Every file carries the mouse PK models of both drugs with their parameters
held at the single-agent estimates, because the authors simulated the typical
concentration profiles and used them as the input to the tumor model.

# Population

All data are preclinical. Experiment a used female CD1 athymic nude-nu mice
(5 weeks old, 17-35 g); all other experiments used male Balb athymic nude-nu
mice (5 weeks old, 25-35 g). Fragments of BxPC3, A2780 or HT29 tumors were
implanted subcutaneously, and mice with a palpable tumor (about
100-300 mm^3) were randomized to a control arm, two single-agent arms and one
or two combination arms, usually eight mice per arm (Methods). Tumor weight
was calculated from caliper measurements as length x width^2 / 2 at unit
density, and the arm means were fitted. Time zero is tumor implantation; the
doses (Table 1) start on days 8-10.

The analysis was done in two steps: the seven tumor and single-agent
parameters (w0, lambda0, lambda1, k1 and k2 of each drug) were estimated on
the control and single-agent arms, then held at those values while gamma was
estimated on a combination arm. For experiments a, c and d the first step was
done earlier, in Rocchetti 2009 (doi:10.1016/j.ejca.2009.09.025), and its
values are reprinted in Supplementary Table 2.

# Source trace

| Element | Source location | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Two-drug grid of states x_ij, growth f_p(w), interaction flux v_11 | Equations 1-3; Figure 1 (right panel) | -- |
| Simeoni growth f_p(w) = lambda0 x00 / (1 + (lambda0 w / lambda1)^psi)^(1/psi) | Equation 2 definitions; growth model of Simeoni 2004 | psi = 20 (Simeoni 2004; not printed) |
| PK: V1, K10, K12, K21, K01 of the eight drugs | Supplementary Table 1 | see each model file |
| lambda0, lambda1, k1A, k2A, k1B, k2B, w0 per experiment | Supplementary Table 2 | see each model file |
| gamma, arms a1, b1, c1, d1, d2, e1, f1, f2 | Results, 'TGI model identification' | -0.88, 8.0, 3.45, 0.131, 0.157, -0.0455, -2.04, -1.05 |
| Residual error: weighted least squares, weights 1/y^2 | Methods, 'Data analysis' | magnitude not reported |
| Dose levels (mg/kg and umol/kg) and schedules | Methods, 'Drug treatments'; Table 1; footnote 2 | see below |
| Combination indexes SC and AC | Equations 4-7; Results | see the index comparison below |

# Structure

With `Ca` and `Cb` the plasma concentrations (uM) of drug a and drug b,
`x00` the proliferating cells and `w` the total tumor weight (g):

* `dx00/dt = f_p(w) - (k2a Ca + k2b Cb + gamma Ca Cb) x00`
* each damaged state `x_ij` (i stages of drug-a damage, j of drug-b damage)
  receives cells from `x_(i-1)j` at `k2a Ca` (i = 1) or `k1a` (i > 1), and
  from `x_i(j-1)` at `k2b Cb` (j = 1) or `k1b` (j > 1); `x11` also receives
  `gamma Ca Cb x00`;
* each damaged state loses cells at `k2a Ca` (i = 0) or `k1a` (i > 0) plus
  `k2b Cb` (j = 0) or `k1b` (j > 0); cells leaving the last stage of either
  chain die.

The PK models are linear one- or two-compartment models written with the
micro-constants of Supplementary Table 1; doses in umol/kg over V1 in L/kg
give concentrations in uM, the unit in which k2 (1/(uM day)) and gamma
(1/(uM^2 day)) are reported.

# Dosing

The schedules below are Table 1 of the paper. Twice-daily doses are 0.5 day
apart. In experiment f, Drug C5 was given 6 h after irinotecan on the days
both drugs were due (Methods), so those two Drug C5 doses are at day + 0.25.
The doses are the umol/kg values the paper prints beside each mg/kg dose.

```{r dosing}
bidDays <- function(starts, ndays) {
  sort(unlist(lapply(starts, function(s) c(outer(c(0, 0.5), s + 0:(ndays - 1), "+")))))
}

doseRows <- function(times, amt, cmt) {
  data.frame(time = times, amt = amt, cmt = cmt, evid = 1L)
}

c2Days <- c(10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16)
c5Days <- c(9, 10, 11, 12.25, 13, 14, 15, 16.25)

arms <- list(
  a1 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC1_gemcitabine_mouse", tmax = 35, gamma = NULL,
            a = doseRows(bidDays(c(10, 14, 18), 3), 29.4, "central_drugc1"),
            b = doseRows(c(9, 13, 17), 267, "central_gemcitabine")),
  b1 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC1_cisplatin_mouse", tmax = 35, gamma = NULL,
            a = doseRows(bidDays(8, 5), 58.7, "central_drugc1"),
            b = doseRows(13, 26.7, "central_cisplatin")),
  b2 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC1_cisplatin_mouse", tmax = 35, gamma = NULL,
            a = doseRows(bidDays(9, 5), 58.7, "central_drugc1"),
            b = doseRows(8, 26.7, "central_cisplatin")),
  c1 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC2_irinotecan_mouse", tmax = 70, gamma = NULL,
            a = doseRows(c2Days, 84.5, "depot_drugc2"),
            b = doseRows(c(9, 13, 17), 72.9, "central_irinotecan")),
  c2 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC2_irinotecan_mouse", tmax = 70, gamma = NULL,
            a = doseRows(c2Days, 113, "depot_drugc2"),
            b = doseRows(c(9, 13, 17), 72.9, "central_irinotecan")),
  d1 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC2_fluorouracil_mouse", tmax = 70, gamma = NULL,
            a = doseRows(c2Days, 84.5, "depot_drugc2"),
            b = doseRows(c(9, 13, 17), 384, "central_5fu")),
  d2 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC2_fluorouracil_mouse", tmax = 70, gamma = 0.157,
            a = doseRows(c2Days, 113, "depot_drugc2"),
            b = doseRows(c(9, 13, 17), 384, "central_5fu")),
  e1 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC4_gemcitabine_mouse", tmax = 35, gamma = NULL,
            a = doseRows(bidDays(c(10, 14, 18), 3), 37.5, "depot_drugc4"),
            b = doseRows(c(9, 13, 17), 267, "central_gemcitabine")),
  e2 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC4_gemcitabine_mouse", tmax = 35, gamma = NULL,
            a = doseRows(bidDays(c(10, 14, 18), 3), 75, "depot_drugc4"),
            b = doseRows(c(9, 13, 17), 267, "central_gemcitabine")),
  f1 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC5_irinotecan_mouse", tmax = 56, gamma = NULL,
            a = doseRows(c5Days, 25.1, "central_drugc5"),
            b = doseRows(c(8, 12, 16), 72.9, "central_irinotecan")),
  f2 = list(model = "Terranova_2013_drugC5_irinotecan_mouse", tmax = 56, gamma = -1.05,
            a = doseRows(c5Days, 50.3, "central_drugc5"),
            b = doseRows(c(8, 12, 16), 72.9, "central_irinotecan"))
)
```

Arms b2, c2 and e2 use the gamma estimated on arms b1, c1 and e1 (the
paper's prediction test, Figure 6). Arms d2 and f2 were fitted independently
in the paper, so their own gamma is set with `ini()`.

# Simulation

Each arm is simulated three ways with the typical values: the combination
(the packaged model), the zero-interaction prediction (gamma = 0; the paper's
"PTGC", the dashed lines of Figures 2-5) and the untreated control. The
observation rows sit on `cycling_cells`, the proliferating-cell state; the
total tumor weight `tumor_size` is returned with them.

```{r simulate}
armModel <- function(arm) {
  mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(arm$model))
  if (!is.null(arm$gamma)) mod <- rxode2::ini(mod, synergy = arm$gamma)
  mod
}

eventTable <- function(doses, tmax, by) {
  obs <- data.frame(time = seq(0, tmax, by = by), amt = 0, cmt = "cycling_cells", evid = 0L)
  ev <- rbind(doses, obs)
  # Observation rows after doses at the same time, so a bolus is seen at its peak.
  ev[order(ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
}

solveArm <- function(name, tmax, by = 0.1) {
  arm <- arms[[name]]
  mod <- armModel(arm)
  doses <- rbind(arm$a, arm$b)
  # Tight tolerances: where the interaction vanishes (arm b2) the combination
  # and zero-interaction curves differ by less than the default tolerances.
  solve <- function(m, ev) rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
  curves <- list(
    combination = solve(mod, eventTable(doses, tmax, by)),
    `zero interaction` = solve(rxode2::ini(mod, synergy = 0), eventTable(doses, tmax, by)),
    control = solve(mod, eventTable(doses[0, ], tmax, by))
  )
  bind_rows(lapply(names(curves), function(nm) {
    as.data.frame(curves[[nm]]) |>
      select(time, tumor_size, starts_with("Cc_")) |>
      mutate(curve = nm)
  })) |>
    mutate(arm = name)
}

sims <- bind_rows(lapply(names(arms), function(nm) solveArm(nm, arms[[nm]]$tmax)))
```

# Replicated figures

```{r figures, fig.height = 9}
figureOf <- c(
  a1 = "Fig 2 top (a1)", b1 = "Fig 2 bottom (b1)", c1 = "Fig 3 left (c1)",
  d1 = "Fig 3 middle (d1)", d2 = "Fig 3 right (d2)", e1 = "Fig 4 (e1)",
  f1 = "Fig 5 top (f1)", f2 = "Fig 5 bottom (f2)", b2 = "Fig 6 left (b2, predicted)",
  c2 = "Fig 6 middle (c2, predicted)", e2 = "Fig 6 right (e2, predicted)"
)
sims |>
  mutate(panel = factor(figureOf[arm], levels = figureOf)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, tumor_size, colour = curve, linetype = curve)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(combination = "blue", `zero interaction` = "blue", control = "black")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(combination = "solid", `zero interaction` = "dashed", control = "solid")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4.5)) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Tumor weight (g)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Replicates Figures 2-6 of Terranova 2013 (model curves only; the figures
also show the observed arm means). Figure 6 shows only the predicted
combination curve and the control.

## Comparison with the published curves

The maintainers read the plotted model curves off Figures 2-6 at the last
day of each panel (or at the day noted). The paper's curves come from the
same equations and parameter values, so any difference beyond reading error
would point to a transcription or structural error.

```{r curve-check}
published <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~time, ~curve, ~read,
  "a1", 35, "combination", 2.41,
  "a1", 35, "zero interaction", 1.75,
  "a1", 35, "control", 3.98,
  "b1", 35, "combination", 3.55,
  "b1", 35, "zero interaction", 4.05,
  "b1", 21, "control", 3.55,
  "c1", 70, "combination", 0.97,
  "c1", 70, "zero interaction", 1.52,
  "c1", 70, "control", 2.88,
  "d1", 70, "combination", 1.71,
  "d1", 70, "zero interaction", 1.76,
  "d1", 70, "control", 2.82,
  "d2", 70, "combination", 1.47,
  "d2", 70, "zero interaction", 1.56,
  "e1", 35, "combination", 2.12,
  "e1", 35, "zero interaction", 1.87,
  "f1", 49, "combination", 3.30,
  "f1", 49, "zero interaction", 2.35,
  "f2", 56, "combination", 3.85,
  "f2", 56, "zero interaction", 2.75,
  "c2", 70, "combination", 0.60,
  "e2", 35, "combination", 1.20
)

curveCheck <- published |>
  left_join(sims |> select(arm, time, curve, tumor_size), by = c("arm", "time", "curve")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (tumor_size - read) / read)

curveCheck |>
  mutate(tumor_size = signif(tumor_size, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    Arm = arm, `Day` = time, Curve = curve, `Read from figure (g)` = read,
    `Simulated (g)` = tumor_size, `Difference (%)` = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # Every arm uses the published parameters as is, so the simulated curves
  # follow the figures to within the precision of reading a plotted line.
  abs(median(curveCheck$pct_diff)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(curveCheck$pct_diff), 0.9) < 10,
  all(abs(curveCheck$pct_diff) < 15)
)
```

The largest difference is the zero-interaction curve of arm a1 (about 12%),
whose dashed line lies a little lower in Figure 2 than simulated; the
combination and control curves of the same panel agree to within 4%.

# Combination indexes

The paper scores each interaction by the time shift it adds. The Time
Efficacy Index of the combination, `TEIcomb`, is the asymptotic horizontal
distance between the combination and control growth curves; `TEIadd` is the
same distance for the zero-interaction curve; and `Delta` is the distance
between the combination and zero-interaction curves. The synergistic index is
`SC = 100 Delta / TEIcomb` (Delta > 0) and the antagonistic index
`AC = 100 (-Delta) / TEIadd` (Delta < 0) (Equations 6-7).

The distances are computed here from long simulations, as the time each
curve last crosses a weight that all three curves reach in their linear
growth phase.

```{r indexes}
crossTime <- function(time, w, level) {
  i <- max(which(w < level))
  time[i] + (level - w[i]) * (time[i + 1] - time[i]) / (w[i + 1] - w[i])
}

indexOf <- function(name) {
  long <- solveArm(name, tmax = 250, by = 0.25)
  ends <- long |> group_by(curve) |> filter(time == max(time))
  level <- 0.9 * min(ends$tumor_size)
  tau <- sapply(split(long, long$curve), function(d) crossTime(d$time, d$tumor_size, level))
  delta <- tau[["combination"]] - tau[["zero interaction"]]
  if (delta >= 0) {
    c(index = "SC", value = 100 * delta / (tau[["combination"]] - tau[["control"]]))
  } else {
    c(index = "AC", value = 100 * (-delta) / (tau[["zero interaction"]] - tau[["control"]]))
  }
}

reported <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~index_paper, ~value_paper, ~note,
  "a1", "AC", 24, "fitted",
  "b1", "SC", 14.7, "fitted",
  "c1", "SC", 29, "fitted",
  "d1", "SC", 6, "fitted",
  "d2", "SC", 8, "fitted",
  "e1", "AC", 10, "fitted",
  "f1", "AC", 14, "fitted",
  "f2", "AC", 12, "fitted",
  "c2", "SC", 32, "predicted from c1",
  "e2", "AC", 14, "predicted from e1"
)

indexCheck <- reported |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    sim = list(indexOf(arm)),
    index_sim = sim[["index"]],
    value_sim = as.numeric(sim[["value"]])
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-sim)

indexCheck |>
  mutate(value_sim = round(value_sim, 1)) |>
  rename(
    Arm = arm, `Index (paper)` = index_paper, `Paper (%)` = value_paper, Basis = note,
    `Index (simulated)` = index_sim, `Simulated (%)` = value_sim
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # The sign of gamma decides which index applies.
  all(indexCheck$index_sim == indexCheck$index_paper),
  # The indexes are ratios of horizontal shifts, so they check gamma, both
  # potencies and both PK models together, independently of the figure reading.
  median(abs(indexCheck$value_sim - indexCheck$value_paper)) < 1.5,
  all(abs(indexCheck$value_sim - indexCheck$value_paper) < 5)
)
```

The paper also says the SC predicted for arm b2 from the b1 fit is "close to
zero": cisplatin is given on day 8, before the first Drug C1 dose, and its
concentration has fallen to near zero by then, so `Ca * Cb` and the
interaction effect vanish.

```{r b2}
b2 <- indexOf("b2")
b2
stopifnot(b2[["index"]] == "SC", as.numeric(b2[["value"]]) < 1)
```

# PKNCA

The PK models are the published single-agent fits, held fixed, and the paper
reports no NCA. PKNCA is therefore used to check the PK layer of the model
files against closed forms that follow from the Supplementary Table 1
micro-constants: after one dose of each drug, AUC0-inf must equal
`dose / (V1 K10)` for every drug (complete absorption is assumed for the
oral drugs), and Cmax must equal `dose / V1` for the IV bolus drugs. Each
drug is taken from the first model file that carries it, at the first dose of
its arm.

```{r pknca}
pkDrugs <- tribble(
  ~drug, ~arm, ~which, ~route,
  "drugc1", "a1", "a", "IV",
  "gemcitabine", "a1", "b", "IV",
  "cisplatin", "b1", "b", "IV",
  "drugc2", "c1", "a", "oral",
  "irinotecan", "c1", "b", "IV",
  "5fu", "d1", "b", "IV",
  "drugc4", "e1", "a", "oral",
  "drugc5", "f1", "a", "IV"
)

singleDose <- function(drug, arm, which) {
  mod <- armModel(arms[[arm]])
  dose <- arms[[arm]][[which]][1, ]
  dose$time <- 0
  # Fine early grid: the fastest elimination half-life (5-FU) is
  # ln(2) / 151 per day = 0.0046 day.
  times <- c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.001), seq(1.01, 20, by = 0.01))
  obs <- data.frame(time = times, amt = 0, cmt = "cycling_cells", evid = 0L)
  out <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, rbind(dose, obs)))
  th <- setNames(mod$iniDf$est, mod$iniDf$name)
  data.frame(
    # pmax(): the solver leaves round-off negatives of order 1e-15 uM once a
    # fast-eliminated drug has washed out.
    drug = drug, id = 1L, time = out$time, conc = pmax(out[[paste0("Cc_", drug)]], 0),
    dose = dose$amt,
    vc = exp(th[[paste0("lvc_", drug)]]),
    kel = exp(th[[paste0("lkel_", drug)]])
  )
}

pkProfiles <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pkDrugs)), function(i) {
  singleDose(pkDrugs$drug[i], pkDrugs$arm[i], pkDrugs$which[i])
})) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(conc))

concObj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(pkProfiles, conc ~ time | drug / id)
doseObj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  pkProfiles |> dplyr::filter(time == 0) |> select(drug, id, time, dose),
  dose ~ time | drug + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
ncaRes <- as.data.frame(PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(concObj, doseObj, intervals = intervals)))

pkCheck <- ncaRes |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  select(drug, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(pkProfiles |> distinct(drug, dose, vc, kel), by = "drug") |>
  left_join(pkDrugs |> select(drug, route), by = "drug") |>
  mutate(
    auc_closed = dose / (vc * kel),
    cmax_closed = ifelse(route == "IV", dose / vc, NA_real_)
  )

pkCheck |>
  select(drug, route, dose, cmax, cmax_closed, aucinf.obs, auc_closed) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    Drug = drug, Route = route, `Dose (umol/kg)` = dose, `Cmax (uM)` = cmax,
    `dose/V1 (uM)` = cmax_closed, `AUC0-inf (uM*day)` = aucinf.obs,
    `dose/(V1 K10) (uM*day)` = auc_closed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # Both sides use the same fixed parameters, so the only difference is
  # numerical (solver and log-down trapezoid): a tight bound is correct.
  all(abs(pkCheck$aucinf.obs / pkCheck$auc_closed - 1) < 0.01),
  all(abs(pkCheck$cmax / pkCheck$cmax_closed - 1) < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

# Experiment c: the printed lambda1

Supplementary Table 2 prints lambda1 = 0.472 g/day for experiment c. The
control of Figure 3 (left panel) grows linearly at about 0.045 g/day to about
2.9 g by day 70, which the value 0.0472 reproduces and 0.472 does not.
Experiment d, in the same HT29 line and with the control curve drawn
identically in Figure 3, has lambda1 = 0.0459 g/day. The model file carries
0.0472.

```{r lambda1}
mod_c <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Terranova_2013_drugC2_irinotecan_mouse"))
ctrlEvents <- eventTable(arms$c1$a[0, ], 70, by = 1)
lam <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_c, ctrlEvents)) |> mutate(lambda1 = "0.0472 (used)"),
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::ini(mod_c, ltumorLinGrowth = log(0.472)), ctrlEvents)) |>
    mutate(lambda1 = "0.472 (as printed)")
)
lam |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 70) |>
  select(lambda1, tumor_size) |>
  rename(`lambda1 (g/day)` = lambda1, `Control tumor weight at day 70 (g)` = tumor_size) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **psi = 20.** The paper keeps the Simeoni 2004 growth equation without
  printing its switch constant; psi = 20 is the Simeoni 2004 value, as in the
  sibling models of the same group (`Tosca_2023_men1611_trastuzumab_*`). With
  a switch this sharp the curves are insensitive to the exact value.
* **Cross-drug losses of the damaged states.** Equation 2 as printed gives
  the damaged state `x_0j` no outflow when drug a hits it (and `x_i0` none
  for drug b), while its cells still flow into `x_1j`, which would create
  tumor mass. Figure 1 (right panel) draws these as flows out of the state,
  so the model files implement them as losses. The two readings differ by
  less than 0.002 g in tumor weight for arm a1, because these states hold a
  small share of the tumor.
* **Unit of gamma.** The Results print gamma in uM^-2 day^-2; the product
  `gamma Ca Cb x00` is a rate in g/day, so the unit is 1/(uM^2 day).
* **lambda1 of experiment c** read as 0.0472 g/day instead of the printed
  0.472 (section above).
* **Oral bioavailability.** Supplementary Table 1 gives V1 and K01 for the
  oral drugs (Drug C2 and Drug C4) without a bioavailability; V1 is read as
  the apparent volume V/F, and the oral doses enter the depot in full.
* **Negative states under antagonism.** With gamma < 0 the interaction flux
  runs from the doubly damaged state back to the proliferating cells and can
  drive `x11` below zero while the total tumor weight stays positive. This is
  a property of the published model, kept as is.
* **Second combination arms.** Arms d2 and f2 were fitted independently of
  d1 and f1; their gamma (0.157 and -1.05) is noted in the model files and
  set with `ini(synergy = ...)` above. The gamma fitted on arms b2, c2 and e2
  is not reported (only their SC/AC, 8%, 21% and 9%), so those arms use the
  gamma of the first arm, as in the paper's prediction test.
* **Residual error.** The arm means were fitted by weighted least squares
  with weights 1/y^2, a proportional error whose magnitude is not reported;
  `propSd` is held at zero. There is no between-animal variability.
* **Single-agent arms.** The single-agent schedules differ slightly from the
  combination ones (footnotes 2-3) and are not simulated here, as the figures
  show only the control, zero-interaction and combination curves.
